newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian finance official doubts 30-yr bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Colombian finance official doubts 30-yr bond issue.

text.p: A senior Colombian Finance Ministry official cast a broad shadow of doubt over plans announced by the government earlier Wednesday to launch a large bond issue with a maturity of up to 30 years in the United States in 1997.
"The possibility of large long-term placements is a difficult one," Clemente Del Valle, the ministry's chief of Public Credit, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"With anything over 10 years the market becomes more exclusive," he added, saying there was only an "eventual" chance that Colombia would float a 30-year bond.

Del Valle, who was leaving late Wednesday for a presentation to investors at Bear Stearns in New York, also said the Finance Ministry had no definite plans to raise up to $750 million through a single debt issue in the United States.

A statement released earlier by the National Council on Economic and Social Policy (CONPES) referred specifically to plans to raise up to $750 million in U.S. capital markets through a long-term bond maturing in up to 30 years.
Colombia issued a 20-year $200 million Yankee bond last February. But a 30-year sovereign debt issue would mark the country's longest-maturity bond issue yet.
The CONPES statement said the government planned the issue in the United States because of "yield curve behavior, liquidity and demand for Colombian paper" in the U.S. market.
Del Valle said the CONPES statement had been vaguely worded, however, and "open to misinterpretation."
